terramare-culture.name: Terramare culture
terramare-culture.summary: A Bronze Age culture, roughly 1700 to 1150 BC, of Italy's central Po Valley, named for the dark 'black earth' residue of its settlement mounds.

apennine-culture.name: Apennine culture
apennine-culture.summary: A Bronze Age pottery style and technology complex of central and southern Italy (15th-14th centuries BC), later followed by the Sub-Apennine phase.

coppa-nevigata.name: Coppa Nevigata
coppa-nevigata.summary: Archaeological site on Italy's Apulian coast occupied from the Neolithic through the Bronze Age, notable for early purple dye extraction starting around 1800 BC.

statue-menhir.name: Statue menhir
statue-menhir.summary: A type of carved Neolithic standing stone bearing a stylised human figure, sometimes showing clothing or weapons.

yamnaya-culture.name: Yamnaya culture
yamnaya-culture.summary: A Copper to early Bronze Age culture of the Pontic–Caspian steppe (3300–2600 BC), known for pit-grave burials under kurgans and often linked to Proto-Indo-European origins.

nuragic-civilization.name: Nuragic civilization
nuragic-civilization.summary: Named after the nuraghe tower-fortresses it built by the thousands across Bronze Age Sardinia; no written records of this culture survive.

domus-de-janas.name: Domus de Janas
domus-de-janas.summary: Pre-Nuragic rock-cut chamber tombs found across Sardinia, quarried to resemble houses and built mostly between 3400 and 2700 BC, some with the oldest known egg tempera murals.

monte-d-accoddi.name: Monte d'Accoddi
monte-d-accoddi.summary: A Neolithic raised stone platform in northern Sardinia, thought to have been an altar, built by the Ozieri culture from around 4000 to 3650 BCE.

castellieri-culture.name: Castellieri culture
castellieri-culture.summary: A Bronze Age culture of Istria named for its fortified hilltop settlements, called castellieri, which later spread into Friuli and Dalmatia before the Roman conquest.

roca-archaeological-site.name: Roca Vecchia
roca-archaeological-site.summary: Bronze Age archaeological site on Italy's Adriatic coast with well-preserved monumental architecture and the largest cache of Mycenaean pottery found west of mainland Greece.

canegrate-culture.name: Canegrate culture
canegrate-culture.summary: A late Bronze Age culture of prehistoric northern Italy, from the 13th century BC, known through its distinctive pottery and bronzework and linked by most researchers to early Celtic-speaking peoples.

ischia.name: Ischia
ischia.summary: Volcanic island in the Tyrrhenian Sea near Naples, inhabited since the Bronze Age and settled as a Greek emporium in the 8th or 9th century BCE.

lipari.name: Lipari
lipari.summary: The largest of Sicily's Aeolian Islands in the Tyrrhenian Sea, with about 12,800 permanent residents and a population that swells during the summer tourist season.

melendugno.name: Melendugno
melendugno.summary: A town and comune in the Lecce province of Apulia, southeastern Italy, known for Adriatic Sea beaches that have won the Blue Flag water-quality award.

latium.name: Latium
latium.summary: The region of central western Italy where Rome was founded; its name, meaning 'wide, flat', is the source of the word Latin.

bonnanaro-culture.name: Bonnanaro culture
bonnanaro-culture.summary: A protohistoric culture in Sardinia dating to about 1800–1600 BC, considered the first stage of the Nuragic civilization and named after the site where it was discovered in 1889.

capitoline-hill.name: Capitoline Hill
capitoline-hill.summary: One of the Seven Hills of Rome, site of the ancient Temple of Jupiter and traditionally seen by Romans as indestructible and eternal.

nuraghe.name: Nuraghe
nuraghe.summary: The main type of ancient megalithic tower found in Sardinia, built between 1900 and 730 BC and now a symbol of the island's Nuragic civilization.

giants-grave.name: Giants' grave
giants-grave.summary: Sardinian megalithic collective tombs built in the Bronze Age by the Nuragic civilization; about 800 have been found, some with entrances like Irish court cairns.

court-cairn.name: Court cairn
court-cairn.summary: A type of Neolithic megalithic tomb with an open courtyard leading to one or more roofed burial chambers, built between about 3900 and 3500 BC mainly in Ireland and southwest Scotland.

el-argar.name: El Argar
el-argar.summary: An archaeological site in southeastern Spain that gives its name to the Early Bronze Age Argaric culture, active from about 2200 to 1500 BCE.

su-romanzesu.name: Su Romanzesu
su-romanzesu.summary: A Bronze Age nuragic sanctuary village near Bitti, Sardinia, spanning over seven hectares with a holy well, about a hundred huts, temples and a large labyrinth structure.

bitti.name: Bitti
bitti.summary: A small town in the Province of Nuoro in Sardinia, Italy, with about 2,476 inhabitants.

norax.name: Norax
norax.summary: A mythological hero of ancient Greek and Roman writing, said to be the son of the god Hermes and Erytheia; one theory links his name to the word 'nuraghe.'

istria.name: Istria
istria.summary: The largest peninsula in the Adriatic Sea, located between the Gulf of Trieste and the Kvarner Gulf, shared today mostly by Croatia with parts in Slovenia and Italy.

polada-culture.name: Polada culture
polada-culture.summary: A Bronze Age culture, dated to the 22nd to 16th centuries BCE, of pile-dwelling settlements across Lombardy, Veneto and Trentino, named after the peat bog where it was first identified.

brescia.name: Brescia
brescia.summary: City in Lombardy, Italy, founded over 3,200 years ago and an important regional centre since pre-Roman times, with well-preserved Roman public buildings.

urnfield-culture.name: Urnfield culture
urnfield-culture.summary: A late Bronze Age culture of Central Europe, roughly 1300–750 BC, named for its practice of burying cremated ashes in urns in fields.

scamozzina-culture.name: Scamozzina culture
scamozzina-culture.summary: A prehistoric Bronze Age culture of western Lombardy and Piedmont in Italy, dated to the 14th and 13th centuries BCE, notable for early cremation burials with ornaments placed in the urns.
